title: Language Groups in Kenya
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Treat every community with respect and never rank them. Groupings are those taught in Kenyan schools (Bantu, Nilotic, Cushitic); to confirm by the teacher for local communities.

skills.key_step: The child sorts Kenyan communities into the Bantu, Nilotic and Cushitic language groups.

floor.prerequisite: Knows communities have their own traditions.
floor.question: Do all communities in Kenya have the same traditions?

representations: a map showing where groups live
steps: Check with a known member of the same group.
contexts: a Kamba and a Kikuyu learner sharing similar words

board.do: Write Bantu, Nilotes, Cushites as three headings.
Add the Luo, then ask for a Cushitic community.

misconceptions.ask: To which language group do the Luo belong?
misconceptions.repair: Start with the Bantu list (Kikuyu, Luhya, Kamba), then name the Nilotes by their lake and plain homes.

misconceptions.ask: To which language group do the Somali belong?
misconceptions.repair: Group by language family, not by way of life: Maasai are herders and Nilotes, Somali are herders and Cushites.

misconceptions.ask: The Maasai live in the south and the Turkana in the north. Are they in the same language group?
misconceptions.repair: Show a few shared words among Nilotic languages and their spread on the map.

misconceptions.ask: Is "Bantu" the name of one community?
misconceptions.repair: List six Bantu communities under the word Bantu.

checks.question: In which language group are the Luhya?
In which language group are the Borana?

skills.key_step: The child gives true examples of how language groups depend on each other (trade, intermarriage, shared skills and languages).

floor.question: Name one Nilotic community.
floor.answer: any of: Luo, Kalenjin, Maasai, Samburu, Turkana

representations: an exchange web on the board
steps: Ask what each has that the other needs.
contexts: herders trading milk and hides for grain
fishers trading fish for farm produce

board.do: Draw a cow and a sack of grain with arrows between them.

misconceptions.ask: A fishing community has plenty of fish but no maize. What can it do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask each group what it has and what it lacks, then join the groups.

listen_for: They compete to be the strongest
misconceptions.ask: What does interdependence between communities mean?
misconceptions.repair: Use a market scene where both sides gain.

misconceptions.ask: Give a way communities depend on each other other than trade.
misconceptions.repair: List what neighbouring communities share: language words, songs, marriages, farming ideas.

misconceptions.ask: How do people from different language groups talk at a market in Kenya?
misconceptions.repair: Act a market with buyers from different groups using Kiswahili.

checks.question: Give one way herding and farming communities depend on each other.
checks.answer: trade milk, meat or hides for grain and vegetables

checks.question: Can one community supply everything it needs without others?
